newsitem.title: USA: Cusiana loadings to rise by 2-3 cargoes in August.
newsitem.headline: Cusiana loadings to rise by 2-3 cargoes in August.

text.p: Liftings of Colombia's closely watched Cusiana crude are slated to climb by two to three cargoes in August as part of a planned rise in production and exports, shifting the supply balance of sweet crude in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, industry sources said on Friday.

"This is going to cause a major conflict and imbalance in sweet crude in the Atlantic Basin," said Ken Miller, senior principal at Purvin & Gertz, an international energy consultancy in Houston. "The Western Hemisphere is going to be most affected, but it's going to have a global effect."
Colombia's state owned oil company Ecopetrol and partners British Petroleum and Total Petroleum currently sell an average of seven Cusiana cargoes of around 550,000 barrels each per month.
In recent months, a few cargoes also have been co-loaded into single shipments of around one million barrels.
A 550,000 barrel Cusiana cargo was last sold to a U.S. refiner at $1.30 a barrel under benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on an fob basis for loading July 20-24.

Current production of around 185,000 barrels per day (bpd) from Cusiana and Cupiagua is slated to rise to about 320,000 bpd this summer with the addition of two oil production units capable of handling 160,000 bpd.
Peak producton of at least 500,000 bpd is expected to be reached in early 1998.
Beginning in July, some of the new production will go toward filling up new tanks and lines along the new Ocensa pipeline system which carries the crude to the Pacific port of Coveas.
The impending increase in exports will enhance the grade's already prominent market position.
Beginning with the July contract that expires on June 20, Cusiana will be deliverable against the light sweet crude contract on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX).
Miller said increasing Cusiana exports are likely to have the biggest impact on competing West African grades.

"Every barrel of Cusiana that comes on stream will have to back out other sweet crudes from the North Sea and West Africa," Miller said. "The substitution barrel will probably be West African, because it's a little more costly to bring over than the North Sea from a total U.S. standpoint. More and more of the sweet crude from West Africa is going to get pushed to Asia."
Cusiana is a gasoline-rich crude with an API (American Petroleum Institute) gravity of 36 degrees and a sulfur content of 0.25 percent.

British Petroleum operates the Cusiana and Cupiagua oil fields with a 19 percent interest. The other private partners are France's Total Petroleum with another 19 percent and Triton Energy Ltd with 12 percent. Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol holds a 50 percent stake.
